**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement contains no audit right binding us. I confirmed this by reviewing all candidate sections (§5 compensation, §8 Client covenants) plus §§2–4, 7 and 10, and by searching for *audit, inspect, records, books, examine, verif, monitor, premises* — all returned nothing.

The only verification-type mechanics run in our favour:
- **§6** — we get supporting documentation for charges on request and may contest them;
- **§3(e)** — we get real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files.

The closest counterparty rights are §8(f) (TrueLink may deploy technical anti-spam mechanisms) and §9 (we grant access for Y2K repairs, at TrueLink's sole cost) — neither is a usage audit, and neither creates frequency, notice, cost or system-access exposure.

Because silence sits above the preferred position, inserting audit parameters would only create a right against ourselves that TrueLink does not currently have. No action recommended.
